headline: Agentic AI booms output, guts office work; 2029 'white-collar recession' forces automation dividends

events: Early-2027 frontier release runs multi-day software and finance workflows autonomously; enterprise agent contracts triple within two quarters
Hyperscaler capex passes $900bn annualised; US grid operators declare capacity emergencies in PJM and ERCOT, power prices up ~20%
Gas-turbine and transformer backlogs push utilities to delay coal retirements; Japan and Korea restart more reactors
Fed holds at 3.5% as energy-driven inflation offsets falling services costs; G20 inflation edges to 3.6%
Big Four, BPO and insurance firms announce hiring freezes; India's IT-services exports stall for the first time in two decades
Second capability jump: agents with reliable computer use and long-horizon planning; humanoid/warehouse robotics scale in logistics
G20 inflation peaks at 4.1% on electricity, chips and copper, then rolls over as AI-driven services deflation dominates
US election fought over 'robots and rent'; winning campaign promises an automation tax and job guarantee pilots
Philippines and Kenya call-centre sectors shed ~40% of jobs; Philippines peso crisis prompts IMF programme
China deploys state-directed 'AI+ manufacturing' push; its export surplus widens, but tariffs stay roughly flat after a US-China chip-for-rare-earths truce
'White-collar recession': US unemployment hits 7.9%, global 7.4%, as entry-level professional hiring collapses even while GDP grows ~2.5%
Mass protests in France, South Korea and Brazil; US 'Hollow Offices' marches in 40 cities; commercial-office REIT defaults trigger regional-bank losses
Fed cuts to 1.75%; ECB to 1%; long yields stay sticky as deficits balloon, US 10y near 4.8%
Egypt and Pakistan restructure; Philippines programme extended; Sri Lanka-style remittance shock hits Nepal and Bangladesh
Rogue autonomous trading-agent cascade causes a 9% intraday equity flash crash, prompting G7 agent-liability rules
US passes Automation Dividend Act: compute/token levy funds wage insurance and a $400/month adult dividend; similar levies in UK, Canada, Korea
Productivity statistics confirm acceleration: US TFP growth ~3% a year, tax receipts from AI-firm profits surge, slowing debt build-up
Data-centre electricity reaches ~6% of global demand; record solar+storage build-out, renewables cross 40% of electricity, but coal burn plateaus rather than falls
Iran-Gulf maritime clash briefly spikes oil to $115 before a ceasefire; Ukraine frozen-conflict armistice holds
AI-designed drugs win first approvals; tutoring and clinical-triage agents become free public services in a dozen countries
Global unemployment eases to 6.3% as care, construction, energy and 'human-premium' services absorb workers, but at lower wages
Top-5 AI and chip firms account for ~40% of S&P 500 market cap; antitrust breakup case filed in the EU
Populist parties lead in polls across Europe; four-day-week laws spread; youth NEET rates in South Asia and Africa at record highs
Global public debt ~101% of GDP, stabilising thanks to AI-profit taxes and lower real rates
Fourth capability jump sparks debate on autonomous AI research labs; US-China open a narrow AI-safety hotline

winners: Frontier AI labs, hyperscalers and chipmakers (US, Taiwan, Netherlands)
Owners of firm power and grid equipment: utilities, nuclear, solar-storage developers, copper miners
Skilled trades, care workers and consumers of now-cheap professional services
losers: Entry-level white-collar workers and graduates in rich countries
BPO/IT-services-dependent economies: Philippines, India's tier-2 cities, Kenya, Pakistan
Commercial-office landlords and regional banks exposed to them
bullets: Output is booming: world growth averaged ~3.6% in 2027-31, with US productivity growth near 3% a year, yet the median worker feels poorer.
Around 145 million jobs were displaced by AI and robotics over five years; a 2029 white-collar recession pushed global unemployment to 7.4% before partial reabsorption.
Compute levies and automation dividends now exist in the US, UK, Canada and Korea, the first new pillar of the welfare state in decades.
Electricity is the binding constraint: data centres use ~6% of global power, utility bills rose sharply, and coal retirements slipped even as renewables hit 43%.
Inflation briefly peaked above 4% on energy and hardware, then gave way to deflation in services; central banks are back near low rates.
Inequality rose sharply as capital and a few superstar firms captured gains; trust in institutions fell to ~31 and protests are routine.
Trade fragmentation is only modestly higher: a US-China chip-for-minerals truce held, but AI-compute export controls hardened into a tech bloc border.
Four sovereign debt crises hit service-export and remittance-dependent emerging economies hollowed out by AI offshoring reversal.
wildcard: A cascade of rogue autonomous trading agents triggered a 9% intraday global equity flash crash in 2029, leading to G7 agent-liability laws.
image_description: In a half-empty Manila office tower converted into a vocational centre, former call-centre agents in hi-vis vests learn to install rooftop solar panels while a tablet AI tutor corrects their wiring in Tagalog.
